summary.headline: KSB H1 FY27 revenue INR 12,920 mn with weak Q1 sales (2–3% growth); management targets double-digit FY growth on H2 export recovery.
summary.overview: Management presented at an institutional investor meet (held 19 Aug 2026) covering H1 FY27 (April–June 2026 quarter as described in the call). H1 revenue from sales was INR 12,920 mn, EBITDA INR 1,465 mn and PBT INR 1,279 mn. Management attributed the subdued quarter to Middle East export shipments held up by the geopolitical situation, supply-chain constraints on castings after gas availability issues, a delayed KUSUM 2.0 solar scheme, and slow project-pump order inflow. Management expects a much better H2 and aims for double-digit growth, though it flagged NPCIL test-bed delays on nuclear and continued fixed-price margin pressure.

financial_highlights.change: Management said Q1 sales grew only 2–3% over the prior period
Well below plan due to KUSUM 2.0 delay
Down from mid-teens levels the analyst cited; management called it temporary

segments.name: Order intake mix
segments.commentary: Standard 51%, Engineered 14%, SupremeServ 16%, Valves about 19% of order intake, per management.

segments.name: Nuclear
segments.commentary: Order on hand INR 1,235 crore covering GHAVP 1 and 2, Kaiga 5 and 6 and the Kudankulam safety package; Shirwal nuclear capacity at 80–90% utilisation with a new shed adding about 7,000 sq m (about 20% plant capacity).

segments.name: Valves
segments.commentary: Margin fell to single digits in H1 on commodity prices, product mix, lower exports and lower sales; management expects a return to double-digit margins.

segments.name: SupremeServ
segments.commentary: Management targets 25–30% aftermarket share in India (group target 35%); business growing about 15% per annum.

segments.name: Solar
segments.commentary: Solar pumps are 5–7% of current order book versus a 10–12% target; Maharashtra tender orders expected to help in Q3.

guidance_outlook: Goal is double-digit growth for the full year; management said 15–17% average growth over time is achievable (10–15% volume, about 15% value).
H2 expected to be much better, with export shipments recovering from Middle East disruption and supply chain now around 85–90% stable.
Nuclear GHAVP testing expected to start in September 2026 once NPCIL resolves test-bed issues; first pump needs about 500 hours of testing (2–3 months), with up to six pumps a year possible.
EBITDA target of 13–14% reiterated; gross margin under pressure on fixed-price project business, partly offset by internal cost reduction.
Export order book about 15% of sales, with a target of 20%.
S/4HANA implementation in H1 of next year, with group cost allocation expected in FY28 OpEx; amount not yet decided.
Capex of about INR 80–120 crore per year (sustenance plus growth).
capex_capacity: Shirwal plant is about 115,000 sq m (15,000 sq m added with recently bought land); a new shed of about 7,000 sq m adds about 20% capacity.
Shirwal capacity about 1,200–1,300 pumps across energy, oil and gas and nuclear combined.
Nuclear: first indigenous pump made in 2025, under testing at NPCIL test bed in 2026; ISO-19443 certified.
Reciprocating pumps being developed under BP&CL technology; EIL approval in process, requiring a running pump supplied within 12 months.
Split-case pump of 10,000 cubic metres per hour under development for export and river-linking projects.
demand_pricing: Management sees energy (thermal, nuclear, renewable) and water/wastewater infrastructure as main growth drivers; supercritical thermal boiler circulation pump win broke an import jinx.
Project market (oil and gas, petrochemical) slowed; Dangote refinery expected to contribute later.
Price increases: foundry costs up 12–15%; KSB standard market price hikes so far single-digit, being phased in.
Export demand hit by Middle East war and earlier US tariffs cancelling some orders; US boiler feed pump orders for gas plants noted.
Data centre: orders from KSB Germany's OEM customers and an international OEM in India for liquid cooling; no size quantified.
Pump content of projects estimated at 3–5% of total project value.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 performance subdued, and how much export was to the Middle East?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the war affecting exports (pumps ready but undelivered) and supply-chain constraints; sales grew only 2–3%, and H2 is expected to recover.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Goal is double-digit growth; nuclear test-bed delay is the main risk, which management sees as low risk. 20% top-line is possible but with peaks.

qa_highlights.question: Nuclear execution and competition for the next primary coolant pump tender?
qa_highlights.answer: GHAVP testing delayed by NPCIL test-bed issues, with testing expected from September; a new tender for about eight reactors (Mahi Banswara, ASHVINI) expected in a few months, and KSB is the approved supplier.

qa_highlights.question: Why valves margin fell to single digits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited commodity prices, product mix, lower exports and lower sales together, and called it temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Why did order intake not improve materially?
qa_highlights.answer: Standard business growing but new-market entry takes time (fire-fighting, marine, mining); project market, especially oil and gas and petrochemical, slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Nuclear execution cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Standard cycle is 24–36 months; deliveries to NPCIL around 48 months from order; management confirmed about 4 years from groundbreaking to first supply.

qa_highlights.question: BP&CL run-rate and scale?
qa_highlights.answer: On track but slow due to PSU referencing and tender requirements; medium-term potential INR 40–50 crore a year.

risks_watch: Nuclear: NPCIL test-bed issues delaying GHAVP testing, which could push back deliveries and revenue recognition.
Gross margin pressure from fixed-price project contracts and foundry cost pass-through lag of 3–6 months.
Export recovery depends on the Middle East situation and shipment clearances; export inventory still held at end-June.
Solar: KUSUM 2.0 delay; solar receivables and state-government payment cycle may keep receivable days elevated.
S/4HANA cost allocation from FY28 onwards; amount not yet quantified.
Q2 results should show whether H2 recovery materialises and whether valves margins return to double digits.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term nuclear, thermal and data-centre opportunities but defensive on the weak H1; management repeatedly says it expects H2 to recover, with few hard numbers on timing or magnitude.
